newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait bourse sets records, but correction seen.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait bourse sets records, but correction seen.

text.p: Trading on the Kuwait Stock Exchange is setting new records this week with the index closing on Monday at a new record high for the third consecutive day.
The index closed at 1,735.8 points, a 0.8 percent rise from Sunday's 1,721.8 record high and a 6.75 percent increase from 1,626.1 points at the end of August.
Trading values are also breaking new grounds, reaching on Saturday a record 63.1 million dinars ($210 million) during the 2-1/2 hour session.
But some experts are concerned a correction will follow.
"There will be a correction, it is only a matter of time," said a leading economist.
A portfolio manager said, "I am a little bit concerned. Some shares are rising without any reason. These firms did not strike oil, so why should their shares rise by a unit or two per day?"
Some experts expect the correction to hit the real estate and investments sector, slightly pulling the strong banking sector down.
"Banks are strong. They have a strong financial base and announced good six-month results," the economist said.

The cabinet on Sunday reviewed the performance of the exchange which officials say picked up due to good economic indicators such as a decline in the budget deficit and confidence in the security of Kuwait.
"It is true that there are reasons for strong trade and good prices but not to such an extent," said the portfolio manager.

Other positive factors included progress by the government in settling the principal on a $5.5 billion sovereign loan and steady repayments by Kuwaiti debtors involved in a programme to repay long-standing private sector debts owed to the state.
Nationals of Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states are allowed to trade on the exchange while Kuwait's foreign residents can participate through mutual funds.
The GCC comprises Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain.
